title: Walking catchment
author: Fieldwork project
description: The ground a person can reach on foot from each site within a travel time, following the street network. Attaches each site to its nearest junction, traverses the streets to a budget, narrows to the wanted time, and draws the corridor along the streets that can be entered. Equivalent to the isochrone widget at its single-threshold settings, measured at 3.8 parts per million on the John Snow network, but assembled from four steps whose intermediate results can be mapped and argued with.
mustNotBeReadAs: Not a service area and not an access measure. The travel time is a street length divided by one assumed speed, with no gradient, crossings, waiting or difference between travellers; the walk from the site to its junction is not charged at all; and the corridor's half-width is a claim that anywhere within it is reached, including the insides of buildings and the far side of walls. The case study it derives from assumed 4.5 km/h for pedestrians in Soho in 1854, and neither that speed nor the 25 m half-width transfers to another setting without being chosen again.

reviews.outcome: Assembled and executed; its members are pinned and its ports and parameters are checked against its graph. Not admitted to the palette: admission needs a human review and an ontology expansion, neither of which exists. Status stays private.

Re-pinned after travel_time_band published 0.3.0, which records the ontology terms it asserts. Version 0.1.0 is kept as tests/fixtures/drifted-composition-2026-10-10.json so the drift report it produces stays exercised rather than becoming a story about the past.
